newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil March INPC inflation rose to 0.68 pct -- IBGE.
newsitem.headline: Brazil March INPC inflation rose to 0.68 pct -- IBGE.

text.p: Brazilian inflation in March as measured by National Consumer Prices Index (INPC) was 0.68 percent, up from 0.45 percent in February, said the government's National Statistics Institute (IBGE).
INPC is based on the spending of families earning up to eight minimum salaries.

The Wider Consumer Price Index (IPCA), which measures the spending of families earning up to 40 salaries, registered inflation of 0.51 percent in March against 0.50 percent the previous month, the IBGE added in a statement.

March's results means the INPC index over the last 12 months was 8.53 percent versus 8.14 percent in February while in the case of the IPCA, the 12-month index was 8.99 percent compared with 7.26 percent in February.
Vegetables were the key factor in the INPC monthly variation (up 19.42 percent) and also for the IPCA index (up 17.49 percent), IBGE said. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
